words.meaning: sharp and critical in tone, often in a clever but harsh way
words.example: His acerbic reply made the routine budget discussion unnecessarily tense.

words.meaning: a situation in which a factor within a system affects both the presumed cause and the result
words.example: The analyst warned that endogeneity could make the training program look more effective than it really was.

words.meaning: unable to mix or combine into a uniform whole
words.example: The two teams had immiscible working styles until the new manager established shared routines.

words.meaning: the practice of exchanging favors or support to advance separate proposals
words.example: The committee chair discouraged logrolling and asked members to judge each proposal on its own merits.

words.meaning: having only one clear meaning or interpretation
words.example: The policy needs univocal language so every regional office applies it the same way.

phrases.meaning: a step or demand that goes beyond what is reasonable or achievable
phrases.example: Finishing the prototype this week is realistic, but launching it too would be a bridge too far.

phrases.meaning: by chance, especially when the result is unexpectedly helpful or inconvenient
phrases.example: As luck would have it, the client was already in town and could meet that afternoon.

phrases.meaning: to stop supporting the position or behavior of a group
phrases.example: Two board members broke ranks and voted against the proposed merger.

phrases.meaning: to increase pressure on someone to act or comply
phrases.example: The lender tightened the screws after the company missed its second payment.

phrases.meaning: competent and deserving of respect in your role
phrases.example: Any support lead worth their salt knows when to escalate a customer issue.
